q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 40 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 40 MPa non-air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.42. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: What kind of tip does the slump-test tamping rod have?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The rod is 16 mm in diameter, about 600 mm long, with a hemispherical tip so it compacts without cutting through the concrete.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 35 MPa in air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 35 MPa air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.39. The non-air-entrained value at 35 MPa is 0.47. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: How is a representative sample taken from a mixer truck for a slump test?
o: The very first concrete out of the chute
The last concrete left in the drum
Concrete scooped from the top of the drum
Portions taken at intervals from mid-discharge
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: ASTM C172 takes the sample from the middle part of the load, at two or more intervals, and combines it. The first and last portions are often not typical of the batch.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 30 MPa in air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 30 MPa air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.45. The non-air-entrained value at 30 MPa is 0.54. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: How is the slump cone prepared before filling?
o: Oiled heavily and set on dry soil
Dampened and set on a flat, moist, rigid base
Held up in the air while filling
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: A damp cone and a moist, rigid base stop the mold from absorbing water from the sample. The operator stands on the foot pieces to hold the cone down while filling.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 25 MPa in air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 25 MPa air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.52. The non-air-entrained value at 25 MPa is 0.61. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: In the slump test, how far is the cone filled with the second layer?
o: To about one-third of its volume
To about two-thirds of its volume
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The cone is filled in three layers of equal volume. Because the cone narrows, equal volumes mean the layers are about 70 mm, 160 mm and then full height.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 20 MPa in air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 20 MPa air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.60. The non-air-entrained value at 20 MPa is 0.69. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: What is done after the top layer of the slump cone is rodded?
o: Water is added to smooth the top
The top is struck off and the base cleared
The cone is lifted without striking off
A second cone is placed on top
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The top is struck off with the rod, and concrete that spilled around the base is removed so it does not hinder lifting.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 15 MPa in air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 15 MPa air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.70. The non-air-entrained value at 15 MPa is 0.79. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: Under the current ASTM C143, how long should lifting the slump cone take?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The cone is lifted straight up in 5 ± 2 seconds, with no twisting or sideways movement. Older editions said 5 to 10 seconds.

q: Which standard governs the slump test of fresh concrete?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: ASTM C143/C143M covers slump. C39 is the cylinder compression test, C94 covers ready-mixed concrete and D1557 is soil compaction.

q: Within what time must the whole slump test be finished, from the start of filling to lifting the cone?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Fresh concrete stiffens with time. ASTM C143 requires the test to be finished without interruption within 2½ minutes so the result reflects the concrete as delivered.

q: What does the slump test NOT measure?
o: The consistency of the fresh mix
Changes in water content between batches
The compressive strength of the concrete
Whether the mix is close to its specified slump
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Slump shows workability and batch consistency only. Two mixes can have the same slump and very different strengths, which is why cylinders are tested.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what slump range is recommended for reinforced foundation walls and footings?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: Foundations are easy to place and vibrate, so a moderate 25 to 75 mm slump is enough.

q: In a slump test, what is a shear slump?
o: One side of the concrete slides off along an inclined plane
The concrete settles evenly and keeps its shape
The concrete does not move at all
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: A shear slump means the mix lacks cohesion. The test is repeated with another sample; if it shears again, the mix is probably too harsh for this test.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what slump range is recommended for beams and reinforced walls?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: Beams and walls have congested bars and narrow forms, so up to 100 mm is allowed to help the concrete flow around the steel.

q: What is the base diameter of the ASTM slump mold?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The mold is 305 mm (12 in) high, 203 mm (8 in) across the base and 102 mm (4 in) across the top. These are often rounded to 300, 200 and 100 mm.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what slump range is recommended for pavements and slabs?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: Slabs and pavements are placed flat and finished by screeding, so a stiffer mix limits bleeding and shrinkage.

q: What is the height of the ASTM slump mold?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The 305 mm height is the reference from which slump is measured.

q: When may concrete be placed at a higher slump than the ACI 211.1 table recommends?
o: Whenever the workers want it wetter
When admixtures raise it or the spec allows it
In hot weather, by adding water on site
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: The table assumes consolidation by vibration. Higher slumps are fine when they come from admixtures rather than extra water, or when the specification calls for them (for example pumped or tremie concrete).

q: About how long is the slump-test tamping rod?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The rod is about 600 mm (24 in) long and 16 mm in diameter, long enough to reach through each layer of the 305 mm cone.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 35 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 35 MPa non-air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.47. The air-entrained value at 35 MPa is 0.39. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: Besides the mold and rod, what other tools are needed for a slump test?
o: A scoop and a measuring tape or ruler
A poker vibrator and a trowel
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: A scoop fills the cone and a ruler or tape measures the slump. A flat, rigid base plate is also needed.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 30 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 30 MPa non-air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.54. The air-entrained value at 30 MPa is 0.45. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: Why should a slump sample not be taken from the very beginning or end of a truck's discharge?
o: They are often not typical of the batch
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The first concrete may be segregated and the last may carry leftover material. The middle of the load represents the batch best.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 25 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 25 MPa non-air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.61. The air-entrained value at 25 MPa is 0.52. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: How is the first layer placed in the slump cone?
o: Filled one-third by volume, rodded 25 times
Filled to the top, rodded 10 times
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Each of the three layers gets 25 strokes spread evenly over its area. The first layer is rodded through its full depth, with some strokes angled near the edge.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 20 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 20 MPa non-air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.69. The air-entrained value at 20 MPa is 0.60. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: How is the top layer of the slump cone placed?
o: Heaped above the rim, rodded 25 times
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The top layer is overfilled so it stays full while rodding, and extra concrete is added if it drops below the rim. Each stroke just enters the layer beneath.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what maximum water-cement ratio is used to target a 28-day strength of 15 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: For 15 MPa non-air-entrained concrete the table gives w/c = 0.79. The air-entrained value at 15 MPa is 0.70. Air entrainment lowers strength, so a lower w/c is needed for the same target.

q: How must the slump cone be lifted?
o: Straight up, steadily, with no twisting
With a twist to release it
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Twisting or tilting disturbs the concrete and gives a false reading. The cone is raised straight up in 5 ± 2 seconds.

q: In the ACI 211.1 table, what happens to the required water-cement ratio as the target strength rises?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.4(a) Water-cement ratio and compressive strength
n: Strength depends on how little water the paste holds. Going from 20 MPa to 40 MPa in non-air-entrained concrete lowers w/c from 0.69 to 0.42.

q: A slump cone is 305 mm high. After lifting, the top of the concrete is 230 mm high at its original center. What is the slump?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Slump is the drop, measured from the top of the mold to the top of the slumped concrete: 305 − 230 = 75 mm.
formula: Slump = mold height − height of slumped concrete

q: What does a higher slump indicate about fresh concrete?
o: A more fluid, more workable mix
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Higher slump means the concrete flows more. If it comes from extra water rather than admixtures, it also means lower strength.

q: What is done with the concrete used for a slump test?
o: It is put back into the truck
It is used for the cylinders
It is placed in the forms
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The rodded and slumped concrete has been disturbed and may have lost water, so it is thrown away. Cylinders are made from a fresh portion of the sample.

q: In a slump test, what is a collapse slump?
o: One side slides off at an angle
The concrete loses its shape and spreads out
The concrete stays the full height of the mold
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: A collapse usually means too much water, or a flowing mix. ASTM C143 is not valid for it; very fluid concrete is tested for slump flow instead.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what slump range is recommended for plain footings, caissons and substructure walls?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: Plain (unreinforced) substructure work has no bars in the way, so 25 to 75 mm is enough.

q: In a slump test, what is a true slump?
o: It collapses and spreads out flat
One side shears off at an angle
It does not settle at all
It settles evenly and keeps its shape
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: Only a true slump gives a valid reading. It shows a cohesive mix that settles uniformly.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what slump range is recommended for building columns?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: Columns are tall, narrow pours with ties in the way, so up to 100 mm is allowed.

q: What is the top diameter of the ASTM slump mold?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The top opening is 102 mm (4 in). The larger 203 mm opening sits on the base plate.

q: Under ACI 211.1, what slump range is recommended for mass concrete?
ref: ACI 211.1 Table 6.3.1 Recommended slumps for various types of construction
n: Mass concrete is the stiffest class in the table (25 to 50 mm): less water means less heat of hydration and less shrinkage in thick pours.

q: What is the diameter of the slump-test tamping rod?
ref: ASTM C143/C143M Slump of hydraulic-cement concrete; ASTM C172 sampling
n: The rod is a straight 16 mm (5/8 in) steel rod with a hemispherical tip.
